airport.name: Dr. Luis María Argaña International Airport

summary: Dr. Luis María Argaña International Airport serves the remote town of Mariscal Estigarribia in Paraguay's western Chaco region. Named after the prominent Paraguayan jurist and politician, it functions primarily as a gateway to the vast, sparsely populated Gran Chaco lowlands. The airport is strategically positioned near the Argentine and Bolivian borders, supporting both civilian travel and military aviation in this frontier area.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Dr. Luis María Argaña International Airport?
A: It serves as the principal air link for Mariscal Estigarribia and the surrounding Chaco region, facilitating domestic flights and occasional cross-border travel to nearby Argentine cities.

Q: Which airlines operate at ESG?
A: Regional and domestic carriers typically operate scheduled and charter flights to and from this airport, connecting the Chaco with Asunción and other Paraguayan destinations.

Q: How large is the airport?
A: It is classified as a medium airport with a single primary runway, handling general aviation, commercial flights, and military operations.

Q: Is the airport far from the town center?
A: Mariscal Estigarribia is a small town and the airport is located just a short drive from its central area.
transport_tips: Taxis and pre-arranged private transfers are the most common ways to reach the airport, as public transport options in the Chaco region are limited. Renting a vehicle in advance is advisable if you plan to explore the surrounding area independently. The roads connecting the airport to Mariscal Estigarribia are paved but can be quiet, so allow extra travel time during the rainy season when dirt roads become challenging.
local_tip: Pack plenty of water and sun protection — the Chaco region's temperatures can soar above 40°C (104°F) in summer, and the airport has limited passenger amenities due to its remote location.
